The approved Day 1 route is built. Participants first read a regression table and practise the five core terms,
then question a claim and judge a fair comparison. Each session has one
two-sided worksheet. The trainer packs keep printing directions, cards and
answer keys separate from those participant sheets.

## Open the sessions

| Session | Length | Content screens | Deck | Participant sheet | Trainer pack |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| What do the numbers actually say? | 60 minutes | 11 | [Open](Oct12_session1_live.html) | [Two sides](Oct12_session1_handouts.docx) | [Five-term key](Oct12_session1_materials.docx) |
| Good news. Enough to act? | 60 minutes | 11 | [Open](Oct12_session2.html) | [Two sides](Oct12_session2_handouts.docx) | [Cards and key](Oct12_session2_materials.docx) |
| Did the programme make the difference? | 75 minutes | 13 | [Open](Oct12_session3_live.html) | [Two sides](Oct12_session3_handouts.docx) | [Key](Oct12_session3_materials.docx) |

Screen counts exclude the title. Session 3 includes a five-minute break.
Session 1 teaches mean, treatment effect, coefficient, p-value and confidence interval explicitly. It uses ten landfill records for the mean and a two-row annual-cost regression table for reading. Session 2 applies these terms to claims. Only Sessions 1 and 3
have a trainer-run R demonstration. Participants do not write or debug code.

Fiona's four-claim triage is retained, with the [existing optional A1 board](Oct12_session2_board_A1.pdf).
The RDD number line, matching cards, ratio wall and credibility grid from the
other branch are already present and will be preserved in later daily rebuilds.

## Try the interactions

Use a choice before revealing comparison evidence. In Session 3, open the trial
interval after reading the point estimate. In each session, select unsupported
AI claims and check them against the extract. A single consistently styled fictional-case notice appears on each title slide. These native deck controls work
in the open page; they do not display room totals.

The course-owned room poll replaces the Day 1 Menti activity. It has a phone
join page and QR, a facilitator page, hidden totals until voting closes, short
anonymous reasons and Before/After phases. [Download the room tool](GreenWaste_room_poll.zip)
and read its [classroom instructions](ROOM_POLL_README.md). This is a local
classroom server; phones must be able to reach the trainer computer. Test the
venue network before delivery. Labelled cards remain the working fallback.

## What has been checked

The three decks were rendered and walked sequentially at presentation size.
Both trainer outputs, evidence reveals, correct and incorrect AI checks and
keyboard choices were exercised. The slide count is 12/12/14 including titles,
with no slide overflow or browser errors in the checks. The lottery can be
drawn twice and its output names manager age.

Word rendered all participant and trainer pages for visual inspection. Each
participant sheet is two A4 pages; trainer packs are four, three and three
pages. The room poll was checked with two browsers, narrow phone layouts,
changed votes, closed and stale submissions, private facilitator control,
escaped reasons and a working QR.

These checks establish that the materials and interactions work in the tested
environment. Classroom phone access still needs a venue test, and the reading
tasks need feedback from the actual room. The participant tasks provide
individual evidence of reading; a shift in poll totals alone does not.
